questions.question: Through which portal should a commercial bank seek RBI approval for assigning additional roles or responsibilities to its MD&CEO or CEO?
questions.answer: The approval must be sought through the Pravaah Portal at https://pravaah.rbi.org.in.
questions.evidence: A bank shall obtain regulatory approval regarding Additional Roles or Responsibilities of MD&CEO / CEO in terms of Section 10B(8) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, through the Pravaah Portal ( https://pravaah.rbi.org.in).

questions.question: Is RBI approval required when a commercial bank assigns additional roles or responsibilities to its MD&CEO or CEO?
questions.answer: Yes. The bank must obtain regulatory approval under Section 10B(8) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, through the Pravaah Portal.
questions.evidence: A bank shall obtain regulatory approval regarding Additional Roles or Responsibilities of MD&CEO / CEO in terms of Section 10B(8) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, through the Pravaah Portal ( https://pravaah.rbi.org.in).

unanswerable.question: How many days in advance must a commercial bank apply for RBI approval for an additional role or responsibility of its MD&CEO or CEO?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires approval through the Pravaah Portal but does not specify any advance-application period or deadline.

questions.question: For an NBFC with assets of ₹100 crore or more that lends against listed shares, what loan-to-value limit must it maintain, and how quickly must it restore the required limit if share prices fall?
questions.answer: The NBFC must maintain an LTV ratio of 50 per cent at all times. Any shortfall caused by movements in share prices must be made good within seven working days.
questions.evidence: maintain a LTV ratio of 50 per cent for loans granted against the collateral of shares. LTV ratio of 50 per cent is required to be maintained at all times. Any shortfall in the maintenance of the 50 percent LTV occurring on account of movement in the share prices shall be made good within seven working days.

questions.question: For an NBFC with assets of ₹100 crore or more, what collateral may it accept for capital-market investment loans exceeding ₹5 lakh?
questions.answer: It may accept only Group 1 securities, as specified in the SEBI circular dated March 11, 2003, subject to review by the Reserve Bank.
questions.evidence: in case where lending is being done for investment in capital markets, accept only Group 1 securities (specified in SMD/ Policy/ Cir - 9/ 2003 dated March 11, 2003 issued by SEBI as amended from time to time) as collateral for loans of value more than ₹5 lakh, subject to review by the Reserve Bank.

unanswerable.question: What penalty or supervisory action applies if an NBFC with assets of ₹100 crore or more fails to cure an LTV shortfall within seven working days?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the shortfall to be made good within seven working days but does not specify any penalty, supervisory action, or other consequence for failing to do so.

questions.question: As an NBFC belonging to a corporate group, what must our group-wide AML and counter-terror-financing programme include?
questions.answer: It must include group-wide policies for sharing information needed for client due diligence and for managing money-laundering and terrorist-financing risks.
questions.evidence: Accordingly, every NBFC which is part of a group, shall implement group-wide programmes against money laundering and terror financing, including group-wide policies for sharing information required for the purposes of client due diligence, money laundering, and terrorist finance risk management

questions.question: As an NBFC, what safeguards must we have when sharing information within our group for AML and counter-terror-financing purposes?
questions.answer: We must have adequate safeguards protecting the confidentiality and use of the information exchanged, including safeguards that prevent tipping-off.
questions.evidence: and such programmes shall include adequate safeguards on the confidentiality and use of information exchanged, including safeguards to prevent tipping-off.

unanswerable.question: By what deadline must an NBFC belonging to a group establish and implement its group-wide AML and counter-terror-financing programme?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires group-wide programmes and policies but does not specify any implementation deadline or date.

questions.question: Before an NBFC transfers a loan account or credit facility to another lender or an Asset Reconstruction Company, what fraud-related work must it complete, and what must it do if it finds fraud?
questions.answer: The NBFC must complete an investigation from the fraud angle before the transfer. If it concludes that fraud was perpetrated in the account, it must report the matter to RBI before selling the account to another lender or an ARC.
questions.evidence: The Applicable NBFC shall complete the investigation from fraud angle before transferring the loan account / credit facility to other lenders / Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs). In cases where the Applicable NBFC concludes that a fraud has been perpetrated in the account, they shall report it to RBI before selling the accounts to other lenders / ARCs.

questions.question: If an NBFC has sold a loan account to an Asset Reconstruction Company, what ongoing reporting duty does it still have with respect to that account?
questions.answer: The NBFC must continue reporting subsequent developments in the account to RBI. To do this, it must periodically obtain the requisite information from the concerned ARC.
questions.evidence: In cases where accounts are sold to ARCs, the Applicable NBFC shall continue to report subsequent developments in such accounts to RBI, by obtaining requisite information periodically from the concerned ARCs.

unanswerable.question: How often must an NBFC obtain information from the ARC and report subsequent developments on the sold account to RBI?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the NBFC to obtain information from the ARC and report to RBI 'periodically', but it does not state any specific frequency, interval, or deadline for doing so.

questions.question: Can an NBFC maintain a pooled account managed by a professional intermediary for a mutual fund or pension fund?
questions.answer: Yes. An NBFC may hold pooled accounts managed by professional intermediaries on behalf of mutual funds, pension funds, or other types of funds.
questions.evidence: (2) The NBFC shall have option to hold 'pooled' accounts managed by professional intermediaries on behalf of entities like mutual funds, pension funds or other types of funds.

questions.question: If an NBFC relies on due diligence performed by a professional intermediary, what requirements must the intermediary meet, and who remains accountable for knowing the customer?
questions.answer: The intermediary must be regulated and supervised and have adequate systems to comply with customer KYC requirements. The NBFC nevertheless retains ultimate responsibility for knowing the customer.
questions.evidence:
(5) The NBFC shall, at their discretion, rely on the CDD done by an intermediary, provided that the intermediary is a regulated and supervised entity and has adequate systems in place to comply with the KYC requirements of the customers.
(6) The ultimate responsibility for knowing the customer lies with the NBFC.

unanswerable.question: How frequently must an NBFC refresh customer due diligence when it relies on a professional intermediary's CDD?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph permits an NBFC to rely on intermediary CDD at its discretion but does not specify any refresh interval, deadline, or frequency.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, what rate of interest applies to a matured deposit held in the name of a deceased individual depositor?
questions.answer: The rate is the one set under the bank's comprehensive policy on interest rate on deposits, and it is subject to the conditions laid down in paragraph 7 of the Directions.
questions.evidence: The rate of interest on matured deposits standing in the name of a deceased individual depositor or two or more joint depositors, where one of the depositors has died, shall be as per comprehensive policy on interest rate on deposits and subject to the conditions laid down in paragraph 7 of these Directions.

questions.question: Does the interest treatment for matured deposits of a deceased depositor also cover a joint deposit account where one of the joint holders has died?
questions.answer: Yes. The provision applies both to matured deposits standing in the name of a deceased individual depositor and to matured deposits held by two or more joint depositors where one of the depositors has died.
questions.evidence: The rate of interest on matured deposits standing in the name of a deceased individual depositor or two or more joint depositors, where one of the depositors has died

unanswerable.question: What specific percentage rate of interest must a commercial bank pay on a matured deposit of a deceased depositor?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states no numerical rate; it only refers to the comprehensive policy on interest rate on deposits and the conditions in paragraph 7, so the actual percentage cannot be determined from it.

questions.question: After an NBFC identifies a borrower's account as fraudulent, what must happen to borrowal accounts at other group companies that share a promoter or whole-time director?
questions.answer: Those borrowal accounts must be subjected to examination from a fraud angle by the concerned Regulated Entities.
questions.evidence: In case an account is identified as a fraud by any Applicable NBFC, the borrowal accounts of other group companies, in which one or more promoter(s) / whole-time director(s) are common, shall also be subjected to examination by Regulated Entities (REs) concerned from fraud angle under these Directions.

questions.question: Which borrowal accounts are within scope of the additional fraud examination triggered when an NBFC identifies an account as fraudulent?
questions.answer: The stated scope covers borrowal accounts of other group companies in which at least one promoter or whole-time director is common.
questions.evidence: the borrowal accounts of other group companies, in which one or more promoter(s) / whole-time director(s) are common, shall also be subjected to examination by Regulated Entities (REs) concerned from fraud angle

unanswerable.question: Within how many days of identifying an account as fraudulent must an NBFC complete the fraud-angle examination of the relevant group companies' borrowal accounts?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the examination but specifies no deadline or time limit for completing it.

questions.question: Do the RBI's NBFC-MFI Directions, 2025 apply to an NBFC-MFI registered with the Reserve Bank under the RBI Act, 1934?
questions.answer: Yes. They apply to every NBFC-MFI registered with the Reserve Bank under the provisions of the RBI Act, 1934.
questions.evidence: These Directions shall be applicable to every Non-Banking Financial Company – Microfinance Institution (hereinafter collectively referred to as ‘NBFC-MFIs’ and individually as an ‘NBFC-MFI’) registered with the Reserve Bank under the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (Act No. 2 of 1934).

questions.question: Under which law must an NBFC-MFI be registered for the RBI's NBFC-MFI Directions, 2025 to apply to it?
questions.answer: It must be registered with the Reserve Bank under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (Act No. 2 of 1934).
questions.evidence: registered with the Reserve Bank under the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (Act No. 2 of 1934).

unanswerable.question: Is there a waiting period between an NBFC-MFI's registration with the Reserve Bank and its becoming subject to the RBI's NBFC-MFI Directions, 2025?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states which NBFC-MFIs are covered but does not specify any waiting period or other timing condition for applicability.

questions.question: Which delivery methods qualify as a commercial bank’s mobile banking channel?
questions.answer: A commercial bank’s mobile banking channel can use mobile applications, unstructured supplementary service data (USSD), and short message service (SMS).
questions.evidence: Mobile Banking Channel – Digital banking channel offered by a bank to its customers for operating their accounts and accessing its services using mobile applications, unstructured supplementary service data (USSD) and short message service (SMS).

questions.question: Under a commercial bank’s view-only digital banking facility, what can it offer in connection with loans or fund transfers?
questions.answer: It may provide downloadable forms for such facilities, but it cannot provide loans, fund transfers, or similar services that create a customer liability or involve moving funds through the view-only channel.
questions.evidence: Note: Loans, funds transfers, and other such facilities, which create liability for the customer and/or involve movement of funds, cannot be provided by banks having view only facility over digital channels. However, banks providing view only facility can provide downloadable forms for such facilities.

unanswerable.question: What minimum number of active customers must a commercial bank have before it is required to offer mobile banking through applications, USSD, or SMS?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph defines the mobile banking channel but does not specify any minimum customer count or other threshold triggering an obligation to offer mobile banking.

questions.question: For an NBFC lending against gold or silver collateral, where must the first auction of the collateral be held?
questions.answer: The first auction must be conducted physically in the same district in which the lending branch is located.
questions.evidence: The first auction shall be conducted physically in the same district in which the lending branch is located.

questions.question: If an NBFC's first auction of gold or silver collateral fails, what options does it have for conducting a subsequent auction?
questions.answer: It may conduct the auction in an adjoining district or conduct the auction online.
questions.evidence: However, in case of failure of first auction, an NBFC may conduct the auction in an adjoining district or conduct online auction.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days after a failed first auction must an NBFC complete the subsequent auction of gold or silver collateral?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph permits an adjoining-district or online auction following a failed first auction, but it states no deadline or time period for conducting it.

questions.question: As an NBFC, how many documents do I need to collect to verify that a sole proprietorship customer is actually running a business?
questions.answer: An NBFC must obtain any two of the specified documents (or equivalent e-documents) as proof of business or activity in the name of the proprietary firm.
questions.evidence: the NBFC shall also obtain any two of the following documents or the equivalent e-documents thereof as proof of business / activity in the name of the proprietary firm

questions.question: For a sole proprietorship customer, does an NBFC's KYC file need the full income tax return, or is the acknowledgement alone acceptable?
questions.answer: The complete income tax return is required, not merely the acknowledgement; it must be in the sole proprietor's name with the firm's income reflected and be duly authenticated or acknowledged by the Income Tax authorities.
questions.evidence: Complete Income Tax Return (not just the acknowledgement) in the name of the sole proprietor where the firm's income is reflected, duly authenticated / acknowledged by the Income Tax authorities

unanswerable.question: Within what time period must an NBFC obtain the two business-proof documents from a sole proprietorship customer while completing CDD?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph specifies which documents may be used and that any two are required, but it states no deadline or time period for collecting them.

questions.question: When an NBFC finances a housing or development project, what must the builder/developer/company include in newspaper or magazine advertisements for a particular scheme?
questions.answer: The advertisement must include information relating to the mortgage.
questions.evidence: The builder/ developer/ company shall append the information relating to mortgage while publishing advertisement of a particular scheme in newspapers/ magazines etc.

questions.question: When financing a housing or development project, what must an NBFC do before releasing funds to the builder/developer/owner/company?
questions.answer: The NBFC must ensure that the builder/developer/owner/company has fulfilled the required disclosure stipulations; funds must not be released until then.
questions.evidence: Further, the NBFC shall ensure compliance with the above stipulations and funds shall not be released unless the builder / developer / owner / company fulfil the above requirements.

unanswerable.question: How many days after a builder/developer/owner/company fulfills the mortgage-disclosure requirements must an NBFC release funds for a housing or development project?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires that funds not be released until the requirements are fulfilled, but it specifies no deadline or number of days for the release.

questions.question: What must a commercial bank have in place to govern all its digital banking channels?
questions.answer: It must establish comprehensive policies for all digital banking channels that account for every applicable statutory and regulatory requirement, including liquidity and operational risk management in a digital banking context.
questions.evidence: Banks shall put in place comprehensive policy(ies) for all digital banking channels keeping in account all statutory and regulatory requirements (including on management of liquidity and operational risks in digital banking scenario).

questions.question: Which prudential risks must a commercial bank consider when formulating its digital banking channel policies?
questions.answer: The policies must address liquidity and operational risks in the digital banking scenario.
questions.evidence: (including on management of liquidity and operational risks in digital banking scenario)

unanswerable.question: How many days does a commercial bank have after the 2025 Directions take effect to put its digital banking channel policies in place?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires comprehensive digital banking channel policies but does not specify any implementation deadline or time period.

questions.question: For an NBFC, what qualifies as a microfinance loan, and which family members make up the household for this purpose?
questions.answer: A microfinance loan is a collateral-free loan given to a household with annual income up to ₹3,00,000. The household is an individual family unit consisting of the husband, wife, and their unmarried children.
questions.evidence: Microfinance loan is a collateral-free loan given to a household having annual household income up to ₹3,00,000. For this purpose, the household shall mean an individual family unit, i.e., husband, wife and their unmarried children.

questions.question: For an NBFC, can a loan to a low-income household be classified as a microfinance loan if it is linked to a lien on the borrower's deposit account or backed by hypothecation of security?
questions.answer: No. A microfinance loan must not be linked with a lien on the borrower's deposit account or backed by hypothecation of any security.
questions.evidence: Further, to ensure collateral-free nature of the microfinance loan, the loan shall not be linked with a lien on the deposit account of the borrower or backed by hypothecation of any security.

unanswerable.question: For an NBFC, what is the maximum principal amount it may lend as a microfinance loan to a household with annual income up to ₹3,00,000?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph specifies the household-income ceiling and collateral conditions but does not state any maximum principal amount for a microfinance loan.

questions.question: A commercial bank extending rupee pre-shipment credit to exporters must monitor the end use of the disbursed funds. What specifically must the bank track?
questions.answer: The bank must track the distribution of inputs by the exporters to the farmers for raising crops, in accordance with the arrangements made by the exporter or main processor units.
questions.evidence: The bank shall also monitor the end-use of funds, viz. distribution of the inputs by the exporters to the farmers for raising the crops as per arrangements made by the exporter / main processor units.

questions.question: When a commercial bank checks the end use of rupee pre-shipment credit, against whose arrangements should it verify that inputs actually reach the farmers?
questions.answer: The bank should verify the distribution of inputs against the arrangements made by the exporter or the main processor units.
questions.evidence: distribution of the inputs by the exporters to the farmers for raising the crops as per arrangements made by the exporter / main processor units

unanswerable.question: How frequently must a commercial bank conduct end-use monitoring of rupee pre-shipment credit disbursed to exporters?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph imposes a duty on the bank to monitor the end use of funds but does not specify any monitoring frequency, interval, or deadline for doing so.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, must I meet the RBI (Commercial Banks - Governance) Directions, 2025 as well as any other legal or regulatory requirements that apply to me?
questions.answer: Yes. A commercial bank must comply with the RBI (Commercial Banks - Governance) Directions, 2025 together with other applicable laws, rules, regulations, and directions.
questions.evidence: The provisions of these Directions shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of the provisions of any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions, for the time being in force.

questions.question: Can a commercial bank treat the RBI (Commercial Banks - Governance) Directions, 2025 as replacing an applicable law, rule, regulation, or direction?
questions.answer: No. The Governance Directions do not displace other applicable legal or regulatory requirements, and compliance with them does not permit a commercial bank to disregard those requirements.
questions.evidence: The provisions of these Directions shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of the provisions of any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions, for the time being in force.

unanswerable.question: Is there a deadline within which a commercial bank must demonstrate compliance with the RBI (Commercial Banks - Governance) Directions, 2025 alongside other applicable requirements?
unanswerable.why: Paragraph 75 states that the requirements apply cumulatively but specifies no deadline, implementation date, or transition period.

questions.question: As an NBFC compliance officer, can our agreements with third-party service providers include terms making them accountable when their wilful negligence or malpractice contributes to fraud?
questions.answer: Yes. An NBFC may include necessary terms and conditions in its agreements with third-party service providers to hold them accountable where their wilful negligence or malpractice is found to be a causative factor for fraud.
questions.evidence: Therefore, the Applicable NBFC may incorporate necessary terms and conditions in its agreements with third-party service providers to hold them accountable in situations where wilful negligence / malpractice by them is found to be a causative factor for fraud.

questions.question: At which stages of the lending process does an NBFC rely on third-party service providers under the RBI fraud risk management framework?
questions.answer: An NBFC relies on third-party service providers during pre-sanction appraisal and post-sanction monitoring.
questions.evidence: The Applicable NBFC places reliance on various third-party service providers as part of pre-sanction appraisal and post-sanction monitoring.

unanswerable.question: What minimum indemnity amount or monetary cap must an NBFC specify in third-party service provider agreements for fraud accountability?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph permits accountability terms but does not specify any minimum indemnity, monetary cap, or other numerical requirement.

questions.question: As an NBFC, what must we do to meet the ongoing due diligence expectations for our customers?
questions.answer: An NBFC must carry out ongoing due diligence of its customers to confirm that their transactions are consistent with what the NBFC knows about them, their business and risk profile, and the source of their funds or wealth.
questions.evidence: The NBFC shall undertake ongoing due diligence of customers to ensure that their transactions are consistent with their knowledge about the customers, customers’ business and risk profile, the source of funds / wealth.

questions.question: When an NBFC reviews a customer's transactions as part of ongoing monitoring, what should those transactions be compared against?
questions.answer: They should be compared against the NBFC's knowledge of the customer, the customer's business and risk profile, and the source of the customer's funds or wealth; transactions that do not match these would not be consistent with the required standard.
questions.evidence: their transactions are consistent with their knowledge about the customers, customers’ business and risk profile, the source of funds / wealth.

unanswerable.question: How frequently must an NBFC conduct ongoing due diligence of its customers under the RBI's NBFC KYC Directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires ongoing due diligence of customers but does not state any frequency, interval, or deadline for carrying it out.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, which party is accountable for ensuring that the information, facts, and figures it reports are correct?
questions.answer: The reporting bank—the commercial bank furnishing the information—is responsible for both reporting correct information and ensuring the accuracy of facts and figures.
questions.evidence: (1) The responsibility for reporting correct information and also ensuring the accuracy of facts and figures rests with the reporting bank.

questions.question: What verification steps should a commercial bank take when providing directors' particulars to a credit information company?
questions.answer: It must ensure that the directors' particulars are accurate and, wherever possible, cross-check them against the database maintained by the Registrar of Companies.
questions.evidence: (2) A bank, while furnishing information to credit information companies, shall ensure the accuracy of the particulars of the directors, and wherever possible, by cross-checking with the database maintained by the Registrar of Companies.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days of identifying a wilful defaulter must a commercial bank furnish the defaulter's information to credit information companies?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph imposes responsibility for accurate reporting and verification of directors' particulars but does not specify any deadline for furnishing information.

questions.question: Under the RBI’s KYC customer acceptance requirements for NBFCs, is it permissible to deny a financial facility to a financially or socially disadvantaged member of the public, including a person with a disability?
questions.answer: No. An NBFC’s customer acceptance policy must not result in denial of a financial facility to members of the general public, especially those who are financially or socially disadvantaged, including PwDs.
questions.evidence: The Customer Acceptance Policy shall not result in denial of a financial facility to members of the general public, especially those who are financially or socially disadvantaged, including the Persons with Disabilities (PwDs).

questions.question: If an NBFC rejects an application to onboard a customer or update the customer’s KYC periodically, what must the officer handling the rejection do?
questions.answer: The rejection must be made with application of mind, and the officer concerned must duly record the reasons for rejection.
questions.evidence: The NBFC shall not reject an application for onboarding or periodic updation of KYC without application of mind. The officer concerned shall duly record the reason(s) for rejection.

unanswerable.question: For how long must an NBFC retain the recorded reasons for rejecting a customer’s onboarding or periodic KYC update application?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the reasons for rejection to be recorded but does not specify any retention period.

questions.question: As a compliance officer at a commercial bank, can I rely on the RBI's interpretation of the Digital Banking Channels Authorisation Directions, 2025 when a provision is ambiguous?
questions.answer: Yes. The RBI may issue necessary clarifications, and its interpretation of any provision of the Directions is final and binding.
questions.evidence: the RBI may, if it considers necessary, issue necessary clarifications in respect of any matter covered herein and the interpretation of any provision of these Directions given by the RBI shall be final and binding.

questions.question: If a commercial bank faces difficulty applying or interpreting the RBI's Digital Banking Channels Authorisation Directions, 2025, can the RBI provide a clarification?
questions.answer: Yes. If the RBI considers it necessary, it may issue a clarification to give effect to the Directions or remove difficulties in their application or interpretation.
questions.evidence: For the purpose of giving effect to the provisions of these Directions or in order to remove any difficulties in the application or interpretation of the provisions of these Directions, the RBI may, if it considers necessary, issue necessary clarifications in respect of any matter covered herein

unanswerable.question: Within how many working days must a commercial bank submit a request for clarification under the RBI's Digital Banking Channels Authorisation Directions, 2025?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph permits the RBI to issue necessary clarifications but does not specify a request-submission procedure or any deadline for seeking or providing clarification.

questions.question: Under the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Interest Rates on Advances) Directions, 2025, may a commercial bank increase the credit risk premium charged to an existing borrower because the customer's credit risk profile has deteriorated?
questions.answer: Yes. A commercial bank may increase the credit risk premium on an existing borrower's loan if the increase is attributable to deterioration in the customer's credit risk profile; a change in tenor premium is also an permitted ground.
questions.evidence: The credit risk premium charged to an existing borrower shall not be increased except on account of deterioration in the credit risk profile of the customer or change in tenor premium.

questions.question: Under the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Interest Rates on Advances) Directions, 2025, do the spread requirements apply to loans that a commercial bank granted under the BPLR system?
questions.answer: No. The spread guidelines do not apply to loans granted under the BPLR system, and those loans continue to be governed by the terms of their loan agreements.
questions.evidence: Provided that the spread guidelines mentioned above shall not apply to loans granted under BPLR system, which continue till date. Such loans shall be covered under the terms of the loan agreements.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum percentage increase in the credit risk premium that a commercial bank may charge an existing borrower under the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Interest Rates on Advances) Directions, 2025?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph permits an increase linked to deterioration in the customer's credit risk profile or a change in tenor premium, but it states no numerical cap or maximum percentage for such an increase.

questions.question: What steps must a commercial bank take before reporting to the IBA third parties it believes contributed to a borrower's wilful default?
questions.answer: The bank must satisfy itself of the third parties' involvement, give them an opportunity to be heard, and follow a due process that is suitably recorded.
questions.evidence: Before reporting to IBA, a bank shall satisfy itself of the involvement of concerned third parties and also provide them with an opportunity of being heard. In this regard, a bank shall follow due process, which shall be suitably recorded.

questions.question: Must a commercial bank be a member of the Indian Banks' Association to report third parties involved in wilful defaults?
questions.answer: No. A commercial bank must forward the third parties' details to the IBA for records regardless of its membership status.
questions.evidence: A bank shall forward the details of these third parties to the Indian Banks' Association (IBA) for records, regardless of the membership status of the bank with the IBA.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days must a commercial bank forward details of third parties to the IBA after establishing their involvement in a wilful default?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the bank to forward the details to the IBA but does not specify any time limit for doing so.

questions.question: As an NBFC, what documents must I hand over to every borrower when a loan is sanctioned or disbursed?
questions.answer: You must furnish each borrower with a copy of the loan agreement plus a copy of every enclosure referred to in that agreement, at the time of sanction or disbursement.
questions.evidence: An NBFC shall invariably furnish a copy of the loan agreement along with a copy each of all enclosures quoted in the loan agreement to all the borrowers at the time of sanction / disbursement of loans

questions.question: Under the RBI's responsible business conduct requirements for NBFCs, is a copy of the loan's terms and conditions required to be made available to the borrower?
questions.answer: Yes. A copy of the terms and conditions must be made available to the borrower.
questions.evidence: A copy of such terms and conditions must be made available to the borrower.

unanswerable.question: What penalty or supervisory action will an NBFC face if it fails to furnish the loan agreement copy and its enclosures to borrowers at the time of sanction or disbursement?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states the requirement to furnish the loan agreement and its enclosures at sanction/disbursement but does not specify any penalty, consequence, or supervisory action for non-compliance.

questions.question: How often must a commercial bank reassess its Base Rate?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must review its Base Rate at least once in every quarter.
questions.evidence: A bank shall review the Base Rate at least once in a quarter with the approval of the Board or the Asset Liability Management Committees (ALCOs) as per the bank’s practice.

questions.question: Which authority must approve a commercial bank’s quarterly Base Rate review?
questions.answer: The review must be approved by the Board or the Asset Liability Management Committee (ALCO), in accordance with the bank’s practice.
questions.evidence: A bank shall review the Base Rate at least once in a quarter with the approval of the Board or the Asset Liability Management Committees (ALCOs) as per the bank’s practice.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum number of days a commercial bank may leave between two reviews of its Base Rate?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires review at least once in a quarter, but it does not state a maximum interval in days or any other precise deadline.

questions.question: How frequently must an NBFC check the UNSCR 1718 sanctions list for updates?
questions.answer: An NBFC must verify the list every day.
questions.evidence: The NBFC shall verify every day, the ‘UNSCR 1718 Sanctions List of Designated Individuals and Entities‘, as available at https://www.mea.gov.in/Implementation-of-UNSC-Sanctions-DPRK.htm

questions.question: What must an NBFC do about additions, deletions, or other changes to the UNSCR 1718 sanctions list?
questions.answer: It must take those changes into account and ensure compliance with the DPRK Security Council Resolution Order, 2017, as amended by the Central Government.
questions.evidence: to take into account any modifications to the list in terms of additions, deletions or other changes and also ensure compliance with the ‘Implementation of Security Council Resolution on Democratic People’s Republic of Korea Order, 2017’, as amended from time to time by the Central Government.

unanswerable.question: For how long must an NBFC retain records or evidence of its daily UNSCR 1718 sanctions-list checks?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires daily verification of the sanctions list but does not specify any record-retention period.

questions.question: For an NBFC, how often must it verify the UNSC sanctions lists and the lists in the schedules to the 2007 Prevention and Suppression of Terrorism Order?
questions.answer: The NBFC must verify both sets of lists every day.
questions.evidence: The NBFC shall verify the aforementioned lists, i.e., UNSC Sanctions Lists and lists as available in the Schedules to the Prevention and Suppression of Terrorism (Implementation of Security Council Resolutions) Order, 2007, as amended from time to time, on a daily basis

questions.question: When an NBFC identifies an account resembling a listed individual or entity, to whom must it report the account details, and who must it also notify?
questions.answer: It must report the account details to FIU-IND and also advise the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).
questions.evidence: The NBFC shall report the details of accounts resembling any of the individuals / entities in the lists to FIU-IND in addition to advising the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)

unanswerable.question: How many days does an NBFC have after detecting a likely match to a UNSC sanctions list to report the account details to FIU-IND?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires reporting to FIU-IND and advising the Ministry of Home Affairs, but it does not specify any reporting deadline or time limit.

questions.question: As an NBFC, what must the sanctioning authority document if a demand/call loan is set to be called more than one year after sanction?
questions.answer: The sanctioning authority must record specific reasons in writing at the time of sanctioning the demand/call loan.
questions.evidence: The sanctioning authority shall, record specific reasons in writing at the time of sanctioning demand or call loan, if the cut-off date for demanding or calling up such loan is stipulated beyond a period of one year from the date of sanction.

questions.question: As an NBFC, what review timetable applies to a demand/call loan, and when can the loan be renewed?
questions.answer: The NBFC must set a review cut-off date not exceeding six months from the date of sanction. The loan cannot be renewed unless the periodic review shows satisfactory compliance with the terms of sanction.
questions.evidence: A cut-off date, for review of performance of the loan, not exceeding six months commencing from the date of sanction. Such demand or call loans shall not be renewed unless the periodical review has shown satisfactory compliance with the terms of sanction.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum interest rate that an NBFC may charge on a demand/call loan?
unanswerable.why: The rule requires the interest rate to be stipulated and payable monthly or quarterly, but it does not state any maximum rate or rate ceiling.

questions.question: What must a commercial bank's Board-approved policy on the spread it charges customers cover?
questions.answer: It must set out principles for determining the amount of each component of the spread, the range of spread for a given category of borrower or type of loan, and the delegation of powers for loan pricing.
questions.evidence: A bank shall have a Board approved policy delineating the components of spread charged to a customer. The policy shall include principles: 1. To determine the quantum of each component of spread. 2. To determine the range of spread for a given category of borrower / type of loan. 3. To delegate powers in respect of loan pricing.

questions.question: How should a commercial bank's Board-approved spread policy deal with the range of spread for different borrower categories or loan types?
questions.answer: The policy must include a principle for determining the range of spread applicable to a given category of borrower or type of loan.
questions.evidence: To determine the range of spread for a given category of borrower / type of loan.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum spread, in basis points, that a commercial bank may charge a customer under the base rate system?
unanswerable.why: Paragraph 28 requires a Board-approved policy and principles for determining spread components and ranges, but it states no numerical cap, maximum spread, or minimum spread for commercial banks.

questions.question: Can a Self-Regulatory Organisation representing NBFCs publish the range of interest rates charged by its member NBFCs on microfinance loans in a particular district as part of an awareness campaign?
questions.answer: Yes. As part of their awareness campaigns, SROs and other industry associations may publish the range of interest rates on microfinance loans charged by their members operating in a district.
questions.evidence: As part of their awareness campaigns, Self-Regulatory Organisations (SROs) / other industry associations may publish the range of interest rates on microfinance loans charged by their members operating in a district.

questions.question: What may an industry association do to discourage its NBFC members from charging usurious interest rates on microfinance loans?
questions.answer: It may sensitize its members against the charging of usurious interest rates.
questions.evidence: SROs / other industry associations may also sensitize their members against charging of usurious interest rates.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum interest rate an NBFC is permitted to charge on a microfinance loan under the RBI's responsible business conduct requirements?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only permits SROs and industry associations to publish interest rate ranges for their members' microfinance loans and to sensitize members against usurious rates; it states no interest rate cap, ceiling, or other numeric limit for NBFCs.

questions.question: When an NBFC auctions collateral securing a loan against gold or silver, what public advertising is required for the auction?
questions.answer: The auction must be advertised in at least two newspapers: one in a regional language and another in a national daily.
questions.evidence: announcement of the auction to the public by issue of advertisements in at least two newspapers, one in the regional language and another in a national daily.

questions.question: What minimum number of newspaper advertisements must an NBFC publish for an auction against gold or silver collateral, and what publication mix is required?
questions.answer: At least two newspaper advertisements are required, including one in a regional language and another in a national daily.
questions.evidence: at least two newspapers, one in the regional language and another in a national daily

unanswerable.question: How many days before an NBFC's auction against gold or silver collateral must the newspaper advertisements be published?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph specifies the number and language coverage of the advertisements but does not state any advance-publication deadline.

questions.question: When an NBFC begins recovering dues from a microfinance borrower, what information and documents must it provide to the borrower and the recovery agent?
questions.answer: The NBFC must provide the borrower with the recovery agent’s details when recovery begins. The agent must carry the notice, the NBFC’s authorisation letter, and the identity card issued by the NBFC or agency.
questions.evidence: To ensure due notice and appropriate authorisation, an NBFC shall provide the details of recovery agents to the borrower while initiating the process of recovery. The agent shall also carry a copy of the notice and the authorisation letter from the NBFC along with the identity card issued to her / him by the NBFC or the agency.

questions.question: What must an NBFC do if it replaces a recovery agency during an ongoing recovery process involving a microfinance borrower?
questions.answer: The NBFC must notify the borrower of the change, and the new agent must carry the notice, the authorisation letter, and the identity card.
questions.evidence: Further, where the recovery agency is changed by the NBFC during the recovery process, in addition to the NBFC notifying the borrower of the change, the new agent shall carry the notice and the authorisation letter along with her / his identity card.

unanswerable.question: How many days in advance must an NBFC notify a microfinance borrower before a recovery agent visits for recovery?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires notice and the provision of recovery-agent details but does not specify any advance-notice period or number of days.

questions.question: Under RBI’s Commercial Banks – Credit Information Reporting Directions, 2025, how frequently must the Technical Working Group (TWG) meet?
questions.answer: The TWG must meet at least once in each calendar year.
questions.evidence: Meetings of the TWG shall be held at least once in a calendar year.

questions.question: Under RBI’s Commercial Banks – Credit Information Reporting Directions, 2025, which organizations convene the Technical Working Group (TWG), and how is the convenor selected?
questions.answer: The four CICs serve as the TWG’s convenor, rotating each calendar year in alphabetical order of their names.
questions.evidence: The four CICs shall act as convenor of the TWG by rotation (for each calendar year), in alphabetical order of the name.

unanswerable.question: What minimum number of TWG members must attend a meeting for the meeting to be valid?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph specifies meeting frequency and the rotation of the convenor, but it does not state any quorum, minimum attendance, or meeting-validity requirement.

questions.question: As an NBFC, what must we put in place to manage money laundering and terrorist financing risks?
questions.answer: We must apply a risk-based approach to the risks we identify ourselves or through a national risk assessment, and have Board-approved policies, controls and procedures for that purpose.
questions.evidence: The NBFC shall apply a Risk Based Approach (RBA) for mitigation and management of the risks (identified on its own or through national risk assessment) and shall have Board-approved policies, controls and procedures in this regard.

questions.question: As an NBFC, what should our customer due diligence programme take into account, and what must we do if our controls are not being applied properly?
questions.answer: The CDD programme should be designed having regard to the ML/TF risks identified and the size of our business. We must also monitor whether the controls are actually being implemented and enhance them where necessary.
questions.evidence: The NBFC shall implement a CDD programme, having regard to the ML / TF risks identified and the size of business. Further, the NBFC shall monitor the implementation of the controls and enhance them if necessary.

unanswerable.question: How frequently must an NBFC review its customer due diligence programme and KYC controls to confirm they remain effective?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires NBFCs to monitor the implementation of controls and enhance them if necessary, but it does not state any review frequency, time period, or deadline for doing so.

questions.question: I'm an NBFC and a partnership firm wants to open an account with me. What documents do I need to collect?
questions.answer: An NBFC must obtain certified copies, or the equivalent e-documents, of the firm's registration certificate, partnership deed and PAN, along with the names of all partners and the address of its registered office and principal place of business if it is different. It must also obtain the documents specified in paragraph 23 for the beneficial owner, managers, officers or employees holding an attorney to transact on the firm's behalf.
questions.evidence: For opening an account of a partnership firm, the NBFC shall obtain the certified copies of each of the following documents or the equivalent e-documents thereof: (1) Registration certificate (2) Partnership deed (3) PAN of the partnership firm

questions.question: As an NBFC opening an account for a partnership firm, what must I collect from the people authorized to transact on the firm's behalf?
questions.answer: The NBFC must obtain the documents specified in paragraph 23 relating to the beneficial owner, managers, officers or employees, as the case may be, who hold an attorney to transact on the partnership firm's behalf.
questions.evidence: (4) Documents, as specified in paragraph 23, relating to beneficial owner, managers, officers or employees, as the case may be, holding an attorney to transact on its behalf

unanswerable.question: How many days does an NBFC have to complete the customer due diligence document collection for a partnership firm before the account can be opened?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph lists the documents an NBFC must obtain for a partnership firm account but states no time limit, deadline or sequence for completing the process.

questions.question: For an NBFC, who must approve the KYC policy, and can the Board delegate that responsibility?
questions.answer: The Board of Directors must duly approve the NBFC’s KYC policy. Approval may instead be given by a committee to which the Board has delegated power.
questions.evidence: (1) The NBFC shall have a KYC policy. The Board of Directors of the NBFC, or any committee to which the Board has delegated power, shall duly approve the KYC policy.

questions.question: What four main areas must an NBFC’s KYC policy cover?
questions.answer: The KYC policy must cover customer acceptance, risk management, customer identification procedures, and monitoring of transactions.

unanswerable.question: Under the RBI’s 2025 NBFC KYC Directions, what is the maximum permitted interval between periodic customer KYC updates?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires periodic KYC updation and refers to schedules more frequent than the prescribed minimum, but it does not state any maximum interval or minimum update frequency.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, what arrangements are treated as a borrower's “credit facility”?
questions.answer: It includes both fund-based and non-fund-based arrangements, including off-balance-sheet items such as derivatives, guarantees, and letters of credit that the bank has extended to the borrower.
questions.evidence: “credit facility” shall mean any fund based or non-fund-based facility, including off- balance sheet items like derivatives, guarantees and letters of credit, which a bank has extended to the borrower.

questions.question: At a commercial bank, does using short-term working capital for a long-term purpose contrary to the sanction terms count as diversion of funds?
questions.answer: Yes. Using short-term working capital funds for long-term purposes that do not conform to the credit facility's sanction terms is expressly included as diversion of funds.
questions.evidence: utilisation of short-term working capital funds for long-term purposes not in conformity with the terms of sanction of credit facility;

unanswerable.question: How many days does a commercial bank have after discovering diversion of funds to classify the borrower as a wilful defaulter?
unanswerable.why: The cited definitions do not state any deadline for a commercial bank to identify or classify a wilful defaulter after discovering diversion of funds.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, what happens to existing loans and credit limits that are linked to the Base Rate or BPLR?
questions.answer: They continue until repayment or renewal, as the case may be.
questions.evidence: Existing loans and credit limits linked to the Base Rate / BPLR shall continue till repayment or renewal, as the case may be.

questions.question: Can a commercial bank's existing borrower shift from a Base Rate/BPLR-linked loan to an MCLR-linked loan, and does that shift close off the existing facility?
questions.answer: Yes. The borrower may opt for an MCLR-linked loan on terms mutually acceptable to both sides, and such a switch-over is not treated as a foreclosure of the existing facility.
questions.evidence: Provided that existing borrowers shall have the option to move to the MCLR linked loan at mutually acceptable terms. Provided that the switch-over shall not be treated as a foreclosure of existing facility.

unanswerable.question: Within what time period must a commercial bank inform its Base Rate/BPLR-linked borrowers about the option to move to an MCLR-linked loan?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph grants borrowers the option to move to MCLR on mutually acceptable terms and states that existing facilities continue till repayment or renewal, but it sets out no deadline or timeline for offering or communicating that switch-over.

questions.question: As a compliance officer at a commercial bank, do the RBI's Commercial Banks (Treatment of Wilful Defaulters and Large Defaulters) Directions, 2025 apply alongside other laws and regulatory requirements currently in force?
questions.answer: Yes. They supplement, rather than replace or weaken, other applicable laws, rules, regulations, and directions in force.
questions.evidence: The provisions of these Directions shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of the provisions of any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions, for the time being in force.

unanswerable.question: If the RBI's Commercial Banks (Treatment of Wilful Defaulters and Large Defaulters) Directions, 2025 conflicts with another RBI direction in force, which requirement must a commercial bank follow?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph confirms that both sets of requirements continue to apply, but it does not establish any priority, hierarchy, or procedure for resolving a conflict.

questions.question: What should a commercial bank include in its loan policies and credit appraisal process so that lending decisions draw on available credit information?
questions.answer: It should include suitable provisions for obtaining credit information reports from one or more credit information companies.
questions.evidence: A CI shall include in their loan policies / credit appraisal processes, suitable provisions for obtaining CIRs from one or more CICs so that the credit decisions are based on credit information available in the system.

questions.question: Must a commercial bank obtain credit information reports from more than one credit information company?
questions.answer: No. The requirement permits obtaining reports from one or more credit information companies, so a single company is permitted.
questions.evidence: A CI shall include in their loan policies / credit appraisal processes, suitable provisions for obtaining CIRs from one or more CICs so that the credit decisions are based on credit information available in the system.

unanswerable.question: How many days before approving a loan must a commercial bank obtain a fresh credit information report?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires suitable provisions for obtaining credit information reports but does not specify any deadline or period for obtaining a fresh report.

questions.question: As a commercial bank, how often must we reset the interest rate on advances that are linked to an external benchmark?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must reset the interest rate under an external benchmark at least once every three months.
questions.evidence: The interest rate under external benchmark shall be reset at least once in three months.

questions.question: Under the RBI's interest rate directions for commercial banks, what change in the lending rate framework is being brought about?
questions.answer: The directions set out a transition from Base Rate / Benchmark Prime Lending Rate (BPLR) to Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate (MCLR).
questions.evidence: C. Transition to Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate (MCLR) from Base Rate / Benchmark Prime Lending Rate (BPLR)

unanswerable.question: By what deadline must commercial banks complete the shift from Base Rate / BPLR to MCLR, and what happens to loans still priced on the old rates until then?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph identifies the transition from Base Rate / BPLR to MCLR and the external-benchmark reset frequency, but it states no deadline, date, or transitional treatment for loans still on the old rates.

questions.question: Are small finance banks, payment banks, and local area banks covered by the RBI Commercial Banks – Credit Information Reporting Directions, 2025?
questions.answer: No. The definition of commercial banks expressly excludes small finance banks, payment banks, and local area banks.
questions.evidence: ‘Commercial Banks’ means banking companies (other than Small Finance Banks, Payment Banks, and Local Area Banks), corresponding new banks, and the State Bank of India

questions.question: Under the RBI Commercial Banks – Credit Information Reporting Directions, 2025, are corresponding new banks and the State Bank of India treated as commercial banks?
questions.answer: Yes. Both corresponding new banks and the State Bank of India are included in the definition of commercial banks and are linked respectively to clauses (da) and (nc) of Section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
questions.evidence: corresponding new banks, and the State Bank of India, as defined respectively under clauses (c), (da), and (nc) of Section 5 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

unanswerable.question: What is the minimum number of loan accounts a commercial bank must maintain before the RBI Commercial Banks – Credit Information Reporting Directions, 2025 require it to report borrower credit information?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph defines the institutions covered as commercial banks but states no minimum number of loan accounts or other reporting threshold.

questions.question: As a compliance officer at a commercial bank, which standardised format must we use to report credit information for the commercial segment?
questions.answer: You must use Form 2, the Uniform Credit Reporting Format (Commercial), for reporting credit information relating to the commercial segment.
questions.evidence: (2) Form 2: Uniform Credit Reporting Format (Commercial) – for commercial segment.

questions.question: What is the name of the standardised, non-proprietary format in which a commercial bank must report credit information to credit information companies?
questions.answer: It is called the Uniform Credit Reporting Format (UCRF), and reporting must follow the formats prescribed in Annex I.
questions.evidence: The reporting of credit information by a CI to the CICs, shall be undertaken in standardised data formats as prescribed in Annex I. These standardised data formats would be a non-proprietary reporting format and shall be known as ‘Uniform Credit Reporting Format’ (UCRF)

unanswerable.question: Within how many days of the end of a reporting period must a commercial bank submit its Form 2 credit information to the credit information companies?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only identifies the applicable data formats (UCRF Forms 1 to 3) and does not state any reporting deadline, submission timeline, or frequency for a commercial bank.

questions.question: As compliance officer of a public sector bank, what is the maximum age at which the bank's MD&CEO or a whole-time director must stop holding the role?
questions.answer: The MD&CEO/CEO or a whole-time director of a public sector bank cannot continue in that position beyond 70 years of age.
questions.evidence: No person shall continue as the MD&CEO / CEO or WTD of a PVB beyond the age of 70 years.

questions.question: Can the Board of a public sector bank set a retirement age below 70 for its whole-time directors, including the MD&CEO?
questions.answer: Yes. Within the overall 70-year cap, the Board of an individual public sector bank may, as part of its internal policy, prescribe a lower retirement age for whole-time directors, including the MD&CEO/CEO.
questions.evidence: Within the overall limit of 70 years, as part of its internal policy, an individual PVB's Board is free to prescribe a lower retirement age for the WTDs, including the MD&CEO / CEO.

unanswerable.question: What is the minimum age at which a person may be appointed as MD&CEO or a whole-time director of a public sector bank?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only fixes the upper age limit of 70 years and allows a bank's Board to set a lower retirement age; it states no minimum age or other age-related eligibility condition for appointment.
